stem: A real-time multiplayer game's backend accepts a custom UDP protocol and needs to handle millions of packets per second with the lowest possible added latency, plus one static IP address per Availability Zone that clients can hard-code.

choices.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer and enable HTTP/2 for the game traffic
Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer and register the game servers as its targets
Deploy a Network Load Balancer in front of the game servers
Keep an existing Application Load Balancer and enable cross-zone load balancing on its target group

rationale: A Network Load Balancer operates at the connection level, supports UDP, scales to millions of packets per second at very low latency, and exposes one static IP per Availability Zone, matching every part of the requirement. An Application Load Balancer parses HTTP(S) requests at Layer 7, which adds processing overhead and does not support a raw UDP protocol, whatever protocol version is enabled. A Gateway Load Balancer is built to insert third-party virtual appliances transparently into a traffic path, not to balance client game traffic directly to game servers. Enabling cross-zone load balancing changes how evenly an existing load balancer spreads requests across Availability Zones; it does not add UDP support, static per-AZ IPs, or the throughput ceiling the scenario needs.
